l: Ephraim, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 9
s: Ephraim is pictured as planted like Tyre in a pleasant place, yet it will return to Egypt, and its glory will fly away like a bird. Its children will be brought out to the murderer, its root is dried up, and it will bear no fruit. It is struck and cast away, and will wander among the nations because it did not listen to God.

l: the LORD, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 9
s: The LORD is the one against whom Israel was unfaithful, and he will no longer receive their wine offerings or sacrifices into his house. He remembers their iniquity and declares that he hated them in Gilgal, will drive them out, will love them no more, and will kill the beloved ones of their womb. He also describes finding Israel like grapes in the wilderness before they turned to Baal Peor.

l: Egypt, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 9
s: Egypt is the place Ephraim will return to, and it will gather up those who flee destruction. Memphis will bury them.

l: unfaithfulness and idolatry, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 9
s: Israel's unfaithfulness is likened to loving a prostitute's wages at every threshing floor. Their corruption is compared to the days of Gibeah, and at Baal Peor they consecrated themselves to the shameful thing and became abominable like what they loved. All their wickedness is said to be in Gilgal, and their princes are rebels.

l: coming judgment, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 9
s: The days of visitation and reckoning are declared to have come. Judgment includes failed harvests, exile to Egypt and Assyria, polluted food, rejected offerings, nettles and thorns in their homes, and being driven from the LORD's house. It ends with God casting them away so that they become wanderers among the nations.

l: barrenness and childlessness, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 9
s: Ephraim's judgment is described as no birth, no pregnancy and no conception, and even raised children will be taken so that no man is left. The prophet asks the LORD to give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts. Even if they give birth, the LORD says he will kill the beloved ones of their womb.

l: The Book of Hosea, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: Chapter 10 describes Israel as a luxuriant vine whose prosperity led it to multiply altars and adorn sacred stones while its heart was divided. The LORD declares he will demolish these altars and stones, and that judgment will spring up like poisonous weeds because of false covenants. The people of Samaria will mourn the calves of Beth Aven, which will be carried to Assyria as a present to a great king, and Samaria and her king will float away like a twig. The LORD recalls Israel's sin since Gibeah, describes Ephraim as a trained heifer to be yoked, and urges the people to sow righteousness and seek him. Because they have plowed wickedness and trusted in their own way and mighty men, battle will destroy their fortresses as Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel, and Israel's king will be destroyed at daybreak.

l: Israel, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: Israel is portrayed as a luxuriant vine that multiplied altars and adorned sacred stones as its land prospered, yet its heart is divided and it is found guilty. It has sinned since the days of Gibeah, has plowed wickedness and reaped iniquity, and will be ashamed of its own counsel. Its fortresses will be destroyed and its king destroyed at daybreak.

l: the LORD, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: The LORD will demolish Israel's altars and sacred stones and will chastise the people when he desires, gathering nations against them. He also puts a yoke on Ephraim and calls the people to sow righteousness and seek him until he comes and rains righteousness on them.

l: Samaria, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: The inhabitants of Samaria will be in terror for the calves of Beth Aven. Samaria and her king are said to float away like a twig on the water.

l: calves of Beth Aven, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: The calves of Beth Aven cause terror among Samaria's inhabitants, and their people and priests mourn over them because their glory has departed. The calf will be carried to Assyria as a present to a great king.

l: Ephraim, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: Ephraim is described as a trained heifer that loves to thresh, and the LORD will put a yoke on her beautiful neck and set a rider on her. Ephraim will receive shame.

l: altars (of Israel), The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: Israel multiplied its altars in proportion to the abundance of its fruit. The LORD will demolish them, and the thorn and thistle will come up on them.

l: sacred stones (of Israel), The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: Israel adorned its sacred stones as its land prospered. The LORD will destroy them.

l: judgment against Israel, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: Judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of the field because of false promises and covenants. It includes shame, destroyed high places, a battle roar, ruined fortresses as at Beth Arbel, and the destruction of Israel's king at daybreak, with nations gathered against the people.

l: sin and wickedness, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 10
s: Israel's sin includes divided loyalty, swearing falsely in covenants, multiplying altars, and persisting in wrongdoing since Gibeah. The people have plowed wickedness, reaped iniquity, and eaten the fruit of lies by trusting in their own way and mighty men.

l: The Book of Hosea, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 11
s: In Hosea 11, the LORD recalls loving Israel as a child and calling his son out of Egypt, yet the people turned to the Baals and engraved images. He taught Ephraim to walk and drew them with ties of love, but they did not know he healed them. Because they refused to repent, they will not return to Egypt, the Assyrian will be their king, and the sword will fall on their cities. Even so, the LORD's compassion is aroused and he declares he will not destroy Ephraim, for he is God and not man. The chapter ends with a promise to settle the returning people in their houses, while noting that Ephraim and Israel deceive him and Judah strays.

l: Israel, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 11
s: Israel is remembered as a child whom the LORD loved and called his son out of Egypt, but who sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to engraved images. The people are determined to turn from the LORD, and the house of Israel surrounds him with deceit. The LORD asks how he can give up Israel or make it like Admah and Zeboiim.

l: Ephraim, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 11
s: Ephraim was taught to walk by the LORD, who took them by their arms, though they did not know he healed them. The LORD asks how he can give up Ephraim, and declares he will not execute his fierce anger or return to destroy Ephraim. Ephraim is also said to surround the LORD with falsehood.

l: the LORD, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 11
s: The LORD recounts loving Israel as a child, teaching Ephraim to walk, drawing them with cords of love, and feeding them. He announces judgment through the sword and the Assyrian king, yet his heart turns and his compassion is aroused, so he will not destroy Ephraim, for he is God and not man, the Holy One. He will roar like a lion, the children will come trembling, and he will settle them in their houses.

l: Egypt, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 11
s: Egypt is the place from which the LORD called his son Israel. The people are told they won't return to the land of Egypt, yet later they will come trembling like a bird out of Egypt.

l: Assyria, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 11
s: The Assyrian will be Israel's king because the people refused to repent. Later the returning people will come trembling like a dove out of the land of Assyria, and the LORD will settle them in their houses.

l: The Book of Hosea, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 12
s: Chapter 12 accuses Ephraim of feeding on wind, multiplying lies and desolation, making a covenant with Assyria, and sending oil to Egypt. The LORD has a controversy with Judah and will repay Jacob according to his deeds, recalling how Jacob took his brother by the heel in the womb, struggled with the angel, and wept at Bethel. The LORD calls the people to turn to their God, keep kindness and justice, and wait continually. Ephraim boasts of wealth gained by defrauding with dishonest scales and claims no sin can be found in him, but the LORD, who brought Israel out of Egypt, says he will make them dwell in tents again. The LORD recalls his prophets and visions, condemns the worthless sacrifices at Gilgal, and declares that Ephraim's bitter provocation will leave his blood on him.

l: Ephraim, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 12
s: Ephraim is said to feed on wind, chase the east wind, and multiply lies and desolation while making a covenant with Assyria and carrying oil into Egypt. He boasts that he has become rich and that no iniquity that is sin will be found in him. He has bitterly provoked anger, so his blood will be left on him and his Lord will repay his contempt.

l: the LORD, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 12
s: The LORD, the God of Armies, has a controversy with Judah and will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds. He calls the people to turn to their God, keep kindness and justice, and wait continually. He declares that he is the LORD their God from the land of Egypt, will make them dwell in tents again, has spoken to the prophets, multiplied visions, and used parables, and brought Israel out of Egypt and preserved him by a prophet.

l: Jacob, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 12
s: Jacob is recalled as having taken his brother by the heel in the womb and as having contended with God in his manhood. He struggled with the angel and prevailed, wept and made supplication, and found God at Bethel. He fled into the country of Aram, where Israel served and tended flocks and herds to get a wife, and he is to be punished and repaid according to his ways and deeds.

l: wealth and deceit of Ephraim, The Book of Hosea, Chapter 12
s: A merchant with dishonest scales in his hand loves to defraud, and Ephraim says he has become rich and found himself wealth. He claims that in all his wealth no iniquity that is sin will be found in him. The LORD answers that he will make them dwell in tents again, and that Ephraim's provocation will bring his blood upon him.
